phase: 31 — validation of the G-A data/authoring route (REVIEW ONLY, nothing modified)
harness: chapter/qa-p31-ga-trace.html — faithful full pass (qa-engine.js node list/order/prevHead) with DOM-ancestry capture on the 14 watched nodes
headline: THE DATA ROUTE IS NOT VIABLE FOR ANY OF THE 14. Every occurrence sits inside button.mcq-option — a region the renderer already declares off-limits to linkification. This is a narrowly scoped renderer defect, not 14 authoring defects.

decisiveFinding.observation: all 14 nodes share the ancestry span.de > span > button.mcq-option > div.mcq-options, and all 14 carry class "de-link" (auto-linkified). None is an authored token (no .rw class).
decisiveFinding.exclusionIntent: chapter-app.js:2818 LINK_EXCLUDE already lists .mcq-options (alongside .builder-token, .builder-slot, .quiz-stage, .reading-passage). The renderer explicitly intends mcq options NOT to be linkified.
decisiveFinding.exclusionMechanism: chapter-app.js:2826 — if (elDe.closest(LINK_EXCLUDE)) return; the test is ANCESTOR-based, evaluated on the .de target at the moment linkifyDe runs.
decisiveFinding.whyItFails: the mcq widget builds its .de content and links it BEFORE the span is appended into button.mcq-option, so at link time closest('.mcq-options') is null and the exclusion cannot match. A detached-subtree ordering gap, not a missing rule.
decisiveFinding.confidence: PROVEN that all 14 are auto-linkified inside .mcq-options and that .mcq-options is in LINK_EXCLUDE (DOM + source). STRONGLY SUPPORTED for the detach-order explanation — the ordering inside the mcq widget was not read line by line.
decisiveFinding.consequence: the 14 HCM findings and their 11 co-located RCB findings exist only because words in multiple-choice OPTIONS became clickable. Every one disappears if the existing exclusion actually applies.

step2_dataFix.verdict: DATA FIX NOT SUFFICIENT — for all 14
reasons: the surfaces are plain strings inside exercises.mcq.options / reading.questions[].options; the mcq schema has no per-word token structure, so there is no property in which to author a role
inventing one would require a renderer change to consume it — i.e. a renderer change either way, but a larger one
the renderer already encodes the correct intent (mcq options excluded); authoring roles for distractor text would contradict that intent
distractor options are deliberately WRONG German (e.g. "Obgleich er ist krank" — option B). Authoring grammatical roles onto intentionally incorrect sentences would teach the wrong thing.

step6_dokumentiert.question: should the occurrence role stay r-verb (part of Zustandspassiv) or become the lexeme’s adjective class?
evidence: the sentence is "Die Ergebnisse sind dokumentiert." — the chapter’s own grammar section (data line 129) and takeaway (line 249) name this Zustandspassiv, describing the resulting STATE
the chapter authors the parallel construction with role r-zustandspassiv, not r-verb
the popup badge "Adjective (Partizip II)" is the lexeme class and is correct
step6_dokumentiert.answer: the occurrence role should NOT remain r-verb. In Zustandspassiv the participle is predicative — adjectival in function. But this does not need deciding: the occurrence is a distractor option and should not be coloured at all.
step6_dokumentiert.preservesDistinction: yes — lexeme class (Adjective/Partizip II) stays on the badge; occurrence role stays a separate axis

step10_crossCorpus.finding: the pattern is the mcq/option region, not the surfaces. Any German word in any mcq option or reading-question option across all 259 chapters takes the same path.
step10_crossCorpus.scopeEstimate: not measured in this phase — requires a corpus scan of .mcq-options descendants carrying .de-link
step10_crossCorpus.globalVsLocal: a renderer fix is inherently global to mcq options but is NOT the corpus-wide guessRole change Phase 30 warned about: it removes clickability from distractor text only, and touches no authored prose, story, reading, grammar or vocabulary rendering.

step12_classification.note: Liebe carries a secondary LEXICON ISSUE (die Liebe resolved for an adjectival occurrence) and Fuß a secondary POS-mapping oddity, but both are primary RENDERER ISSUE because the words should not be clickable in option text.

proposedEditsIfApproved.route: RENDERER — make the existing .mcq-options exclusion effective
candidateShapes: link the mcq option content only AFTER it is attached to button.mcq-option (so closest() can see the ancestor), or
pass the option host to linkifyDe and let the ancestor test run against the attached tree, or
check the exclusion on the text-node host as well as the .de target
proposedEditsIfApproved.regressionRisk: MEDIUM — removes clickability from all mcq/option German text corpus-wide. That is the renderer’s stated intent, but it changes learner-facing interactivity, so it needs a full before/after sweep and a product decision: should distractor words be tappable at all?
proposedEditsIfApproved.notProposedForApproval: no edit is proposed in this phase; the decision above is a product call, not a QA call
